paths.title: Cancellation replay violates the one-refund invariant
paths.persona: Authenticated customer with one payable order
paths.precondition: The customer can replay cancellation for the same order.
steps: orders.py:6-8 accepts cancellation without checking prior state and overwrites it unconditionally.
orders.py:9 invokes credit on every replay.
ledger.py:8 appends a new credit record without deduplicating the order reference.
evidence: No state comparison precedes credit(order['account'], order['total'], order['id']).
CREDITS.append(record) executes for every call at ledger.py:8.
paths.impact: Repeated credits for one purchase corrupt balances and permit financial abuse.
mitigations: Require a PENDING to CANCELLED transition and make ledger credit idempotent by order ID.
paths.analysis: The second and later cancellation calls follow exactly the same reachable credit path as the first.
paths.defense: None; setting CANCELLED does not gate the operation.
paths.remediation: Atomically enforce the state invariant and add a uniqueness constraint for refund references.
paths.remediation_risks: Retries must return the original result rather than fail or issue another credit.
paths.validation: Call cancellation twice concurrently and sequentially; exactly one ledger credit must exist.
